title: Linked List
hints: Walking the list uses raw pointers that do not own anything (`Node*` from `.get()`); owning happens only through the `unique_ptr`s. `push_back` walks to the last node, then sets its `next`.
`reverse` keeps a `std::unique_ptr<Node> previous{}`; for each node, take its `next` out, point it at `previous`, and make the node the new `previous`. At the end, `previous` is the new head.
requirements: `struct Node { int value; std::unique_ptr<Node> next; };` and a `LinkedList` class that owns the head
`reverse()` that relinks the nodes (no new nodes)
The destructor frees the nodes in a loop, not by recursion (a 100,000-node list would overflow the stack otherwise)
stretch: A second version with raw `Node*` and manual `delete`, a deep copy constructor, and an iterator so range-for works.
